slides.7.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
slides.7.questions.0.question: What does the letter 'G' in DOCG stand for?
slides.7.questions.0.explanation: The 'G' in DOCG stands for Garantita (Guaranteed), meaning that beyond the controlled origin, there is also an official state guarantee of quality — Italy's strictest wine classification.
slides.7.questions.1.question: Why were Super Tuscans originally labelled as IGT? (Multiple choice)
slides.7.questions.1.options.0: A. They used non-approved varieties such as Cabernet Sauvignon
slides.7.questions.1.options.1: B. Winemakers deliberately chose a lower tier to sell cheaply
slides.7.questions.1.options.2: C. The DOC rules at the time banned non-traditional varieties
slides.7.questions.1.options.3: D. IGT had better market recognition than DOC
slides.7.questions.1.explanation: In the 1980s, winemakers wanted to use Cabernet Sauvignon and similar varieties, but DOC rules restricted wines to traditional varieties. Hence IGT was the only option. Later Sassicaia earned its own DOC.
slides.7.questions.2.question: Approximately how many DOCGs does Italy currently have?
slides.7.questions.2.explanation: Italy currently has over 77 DOCG zones, concentrated mainly in Piemonte (18 DOCGs), Tuscany and Veneto — and the number continues to grow.
slides.7.questions.3.question: Which classification tier gives winemakers the greatest creative freedom in grape varieties and techniques?
slides.7.questions.3.explanation: IGT (Indicazione Geografica Tipica) is the least restrictive of the four tiers, allowing any variety and winemaking technique. Many innovative premium wines like the Super Tuscans choose the IGT designation.
slides.7.questions.4.question: Which of the following must legally appear on an Italian wine label? (Multiple choice)
slides.7.questions.4.explanation: Producer name, classification tier, and vintage must all appear on the label — these are the essential identifiers of an Italian wine. Retail price is not legally required and is set by the market.

quiz.0.question: What is the full English name of DOCG?
quiz.0.options.1: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita
quiz.0.explanation: DOCG stands for Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, meaning 'Guaranteed Designation of Controlled Origin'.
quiz.1.question: How many DOCG zones does Italy currently have?
quiz.1.explanation: Italy currently has 74 DOCG zones — the highest classification tier in Italian wine.
quiz.2.question: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for DOCG?
quiz.2.options.0: Must have been DOC for at least 5 years
quiz.2.options.1: Numbered official neck band on every bottle
quiz.2.options.3: Must pass chemical analysis and sensory evaluation
quiz.2.explanation: DOCG typically emphasises indigenous varieties; using international varieties is not a requirement.
quiz.3.question: IGT is equivalent to which French classification?
quiz.3.explanation: IGT (Indicazione Geografica Tipica) is equivalent to France's IGP (Indication Géographique Protégée).
